newsitem.title: USA: Freeport sees long-term fertilizer sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Freeport sees long-term fertilizer sales growth.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP said Tuesday the long-term, fundamental market outlook for phosphate fertilizers remains favorable because of low global grain stocks and high grain prices.

Global fertilizer demand is expected to continue to rise as a result of increased fertilizer applications and as additional acreage is planted to provide basic food production for increasing world populations and improving dietary standards, the company explained.
The partnership said IMC-Agrico will continue to monitor market conditions and make production adjustments.
IMC-Agrico is a joint venture between IMC Global Inc and Freeport Resource, which is 51 percent owned by Freeport-McMoRan Inc.

The third quarter of 1996 began with unseasonably high domestic shipments of phosphate fertilizers and sizable purchases of DAP by India and Pakistan, which led IMC-Agrico to resume full capacity operations at its New Wales, Fla., plant and to commence production at its Taft, La., plant in July. A lull in domestic demand, combined with record industry-wide production, prompted IMC-Agrico again to suspend temporarily Taft production at quarter-end.

Freeport-Resource said its diammonium phosphate price realizations for the third quarter averaged about 4 percent higher than year-ago levels but these benefits were offset by a 12 percent decrease in phosphate fertilizer sales volumes.
Unit production costs were slightly less than year ago amounts because of lower costs for ammonia and sulphur, partially offset by higher rock production and natural gas costs, the company said.
It said phosphate rock price realizations of $24.73 per ton for the third quarter of 1996 were higher than the 1995 period.
But the improved prices were offset by lower sales volumes and higher rock mining costs, resulting in lower operating earnings.
IMC-Agrico will continue to reduce rock sales volumes to third parties in order to maximize the long term value of its reserves through internal use, Freeport said.

The company said its Main Pass and Culberson sulphur mines continued to operate at reduced rates (equivalent to 350,000 tons lower annual production) during the latest quarter in response to lower domestic sulphur demand from phosphate fertilizer producers.

Sulphur market prices in the quarter were hurt by the lower demand, the company said. Movement of Canadian sulphur to the U.S. market fell during the quarter in tandem with lower prices and exporters' concerns over recent anti-dumping actions taken by the U.S. Department of Commerce.
